```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# HTML figures are drawn as PNG and kept as WebP: lossless, or lossy at quality 90 when that is less than half the
# size. The PDF figures stay vector graphics. Any failure of magick (not installed, no WebP, or a broken
# installation whose system libraries are missing) keeps the PNG
webp <- function(path) {
  if (knitr::is_latex_output() || !grepl(pattern = "[.]png$", x = path)) return(path)
  tryCatch(
      {
        if (!requireNamespace("magick", quietly = TRUE) || !isTRUE(magick::magick_config()$webp)) return(path)
        img <- magick::image_read(path)
        out <- sub(pattern = "[.]png$", replacement = ".webp", x = path)
        tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".webp")
        magick::image_write(
            image   = img
          , path    = out
          , format  = "webp"
          , quality = 100
          , defines = c(`webp:lossless` = "true")
          )
        magick::image_write(image = img, path = tmp, format = "webp", quality = 90)
        if (file.size(tmp) < file.size(out) / 2) file.copy(from = tmp, to = out, overwrite = TRUE)
        unlink(c(path, tmp))
        out
      }
    , error = function(e) path
    )
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = FALSE, comment = "", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.2,
                      dev = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "cairo_pdf" else "ragg_png", dpi = 96,
                      fig.process = webp)
if (requireNamespace("VetResearchLMM", quietly = TRUE)) library(VetResearchLMM) else
  pkgload::load_all(export_all = FALSE, helpers = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
```


# Abstract

`vlm_app()` opens a point-and-click application in the web browser. It needs the packages **shiny**, **bslib** and
**DT**. Every example of the book loads with one click, and every result comes with a plain-language
interpretation, the printed output, tables to copy or download, plots and the R code that repeats the analysis.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
vlm_app(
    launch.browser = TRUE
  )
```

# Pages

* **Data**: the ten data sets of the book or a CSV file.
* **Model**: fixed effects, random variance components, random coefficients per subject, a residual structure,
  estimation method, denominator degrees of freedom and test type. *Load an example of the book* fills every field
  for one of the 17 analyses of the book.
* **Means**: least-squares means and their differences with Tukey, Bonferroni or Sidak adjustment.
* **Estimates**: estimates and contrasts typed as in SAS, one per line, for example
  `Samorin mean: intercept 1 Drug 0 1 dose 0.5 0.5 Drug:dose 0 0 0.5 0.5`.
* **Random effects**: best linear unbiased predictions.
* **Expected mean squares**: the analysis of variance of PROC GLM with a RANDOM statement.
* **Compare**: independent, compound symmetry, AR(1) and random coefficient structures for the fixed effects of the
  Model page.

```{r fig-model, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "The Model page with Example 3.3, Model 3."}
knitr::include_graphics(path = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "figures/app-model.jpg" else "figures/app-model.webp")
```

```{r fig-means, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "The Means page with Tukey-Kramer comparisons."}
knitr::include_graphics(path = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "figures/app-means.jpg" else "figures/app-means.webp")
```

# Deployment

`vlm_app_object()` returns the application object, for example for a file `app.R` on a server:
`library(VetResearchLMM); vlm_app_object()`.
